item.title: Mark Bezos’ Fund Faces Fight to Recoup Losses From Fence Startup
item.description: A venture capital firm co-founded by Jeff Bezos’ younger brother Mark sank $11.7 million into a startup that fashioned itself as an Uber of fence installation. Now it’s suing the startup’s founder after the company’s collapse amid allegations of fraud and mismanagement.

item.title: New York City’s Five Pensions Gain 13% on Surging US Stocks
item.description: New York City’s five pensions beat their investment target over the past fiscal year, propelled by a record-breaking US stock market.

item.title: Nvidia-Backed Startup CodeRabbit Valued at $1.5 Billion in Round
item.description: CodeRabbit Inc., an artificial intelligence-powered code review service, has raised $143 million in a new funding round, tapping into demand for tools to spot flaws in AI-generated software programming.

item.title: Bond Traders Keep Cointoss Wager on September Fed Hike Post-CPI
item.description: Traders held on to their hedges that Federal Reserve officials could raise interest rates at their next meeting in September, pricing in a roughly 50% chance of a move after a tame reading of US inflation.

item.title: Whoop Plans to Double Size of Boston Headquarters Ahead of IPO
item.description: Whoop Inc., the maker of popular screenless fitness trackers, plans to roughly double the size of its Boston headquarters, boosting a city struggling to grab a bigger piece of the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Real Estate Fund Set to Lose Boston Life Science Investment
item.description: A small US commercial real estate fund run by Deutsche Finance Group, the asset manager tied to many of the soured deals at German pension fund BVK, plans to file for insolvency after its investment in a Boston life sciences complex soured.

item.title: Hormuz Closure Helps Emerging-Market Company Bonds Beat US Peers
item.description: The average borrowing cost of emerging-market companies has fallen to the lowest level since January relative to US corporates as global bond investors’ diversification into higher-yielding assets drives an outperformance.

item.title: US Core Inflation Comes in Subdued, Easing Pressure on Fed
item.description: Underlying US inflation was subdued in July, likely easing pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates.

item.title: Potential ‘Peak Earnings’ Set the Stage for Disappointing Stocks
item.description: The latest reason to worry about the stock market is quite the doozy: Earnings growth has been too strong.

item.title: Vestas CEO Says EU Prevents Mergers Needed to Compete Globally
item.description: Europe’s wind turbine makers would be better able to compete globally if regulators in Brussels allowed more consolidation, according to the chief executive officer of Vestas Wind Systems A/S.

item.title: WeRide Tops Estimates on Surging Domestic Ride-Hailing Demand
item.description: WeRide Inc. sales beat expectations, powered by surging domestic ride-hailing demand and accelerated expansion in Europe.

item.title: US Stock Futures Rise as Tech Rally Resumes Before Key CPI Data
item.description: US stock futures are up before the bell as traders await key inflation data that will provide insight into the next leg of the rally, after recent earnings revived optimism over the artificial intelligence buildout.

item.title: US Stock Futures Today: Borr, Cava, CoreWeave, ERock, Super Micro
item.description: S&P 500 Index futures are up 0.3% as of 7:59 a.m. in New York. Upbeat results from AI infrastructure firms revived appetite for tech stocks with traders awaiting a key US inflation reading later Wednesday.

item.title: Saudis Report Million-Barrel Output Rebound in July to OPEC
item.description: Saudi Arabia reported to OPEC that it increased crude oil production by just over 1 million barrels a day last month, a reflection of the recovery among Persian Gulf producers during a brief ceasefire in the Iran war.

item.title: Swiss Bankers Face Mandatory Bonus Deferral Under Reform
item.description: The Swiss government wants to enshrine in law the deferral of top bankers’ bonuses for a number of years, as part of a package aimed at shoring up financial regulation following the collapse of Credit Suisse.

item.title: Nebius Reports 514% Jump in AI Cloud Sales as Demand Booms
item.description: Nebius Group NV reported a 514% jump in second-quarter sales for its cloud business following strong demand for AI computing power.

item.title: Tata Group Erases $4.5 Billion in Value as Chairman Plans Exit
item.description: Shares of India’s Tata Group companies wiped out 433 billion rupees ($4.5 billion) in market value Wednesday after Chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran said he will step down when his term ends in February, deepening a leadership crisis.

item.title: Norway Oil Fund CEO Says He’s More Nervous After Record Returns
item.description: A record first-half return for Norway’s $2.3 trillion sovereign wealth fund is “as good as it gets,” its chief executive officer said.

item.title: Guinea Eyes Simandou Revenue Surge With New IMF Loan Program
item.description: Guinea expects a proposed $425 million International Monetary Fund program to boost income from its Simandou iron-ore project and the broader mining industry, the nation’s finance minister said.

item.title: Jumia Wins IFC, Axian Backing in $50 Million Equity Fundraising
item.description: Jumia Technologies AG secured $50 million in fresh equity funding from its biggest shareholder and the World Bank’s International Finance Corp. as the African e-commerce company pushes toward its first profit.

item.title: China’s Stubborn Commodity Markets Defy Economic Rulebook
item.description: By surviving on lower prices, producers are complicating Beijing’s struggle with weak inflation.

item.description: Investors seek evidence of Tencent closing the gap on AI leaders

item.title: US tariffs and enforcement and CBP
item.description: Most American importers play by the rules and pay tariffs, but others find ways around full compliance

item.title: China steps up tax collection push, targets mega rich in sign of fiscal worry
item.description: Beijing has stepped up efforts on offshore trusts, clamping down on a structure the country’s mega-rich used to invest billions abroad.

item.title: Market’s Momentum Darlings Resurface as Optical Stocks Take Off
item.description: One of the stock market’s favorite momentum plays from earlier this year is re-emerging as rising confidence in artificial intelligence spending sends the shares of optical component makers soaring again.

item.title: India Inflation Stays Within Target Band, Backs RBI Pause
item.description: India’s inflation was broadly steady in July, holding within the Reserve Bank’s 2%-6% target range and cementing expectations policymakers will keep interest rates unchanged for some time.

item.title: AI Is Creating a New Path for Musical Stardom, With Uncertain Staying Power
item.description: Are AI-aided music creators like “Saxboy Billy” one-hit wonders?

item.title: MEMX Files to List Prediction Market-Style Bets on Earnings
item.description: Exchange operator MEMX is looking to become the latest financial exchange to compete with prediction markets by offering binary bets on corporate earnings metrics, according to a representative for the company.

item.title: Emerging Stocks Rise on Tech as Currency Traders Await US CPI
item.description: Emerging-market stocks rose, led by a rally in Asian chipmakers as upbeat results from AI infrastructure firms revived appetite for tech stocks. Developing-nation currencies were mixed before the publication of US inflation data later in the session.
